text: How does a plant 'variation potential' differ from a plant action potential?
choices: It is a faster, all-or-nothing electrical spike strictly confined to the phloem
It is identical in mechanism to an animal neuronal action potential
It is a slow, graded depolarization driven by hydraulic pressure changes in the xylem
It is a purely chemical signal with no electrical component at all
explanation: The variation potential is a slow, graded depolarization driven by a xylem pressure (hydraulic) wave that activates mechanosensitive channels, so it is not the all-or-nothing, electrically stereotyped phloem action potential (choice 0). It is not mechanistically identical to an animal action potential (choice 1), and it does have an electrical component (choice 3).
